paste.helpBody:
Paste whatever you have: a list of titles, a team-by-team breakdown, or a column from a spreadsheet. We group them into role families, match each role to a track, and add them to families you already have where they fit. Nothing is saved until you confirm.

A role family groups roles that share the same kind of work, like Engineering or Sales; families organize the register and never affect the weighting. A track is the kind of job, for example individual contributor or manager; it says nothing about seniority.

payPolicy.question: Are the pay policy and pay-setting criteria gender-neutral, and are they clear to those who apply them?
payPolicy.helper: Look at how pay decisions are actually made in practice, not only what is written down.

collectiveAgreements.title: Collective agreements
collectiveAgreements.question: Are collective agreements and local pay agreements applied the same way for women and men?
collectiveAgreements.helper: Check both the agreement's terms and how they are used in day-to-day pay decisions.

benefits.title: Benefits and variable pay
benefits.question: Are benefits, allowances and variable pay granted on gender-neutral grounds?
benefits.helper: Include bonuses, car allowances, on-call pay and other extras alongside base pay.

payPractices.title: Pay-setting practice
payPractices.question: Is pay-setting practice gender-neutral at hiring, promotion and during parental leave?
payPractices.helper: A pay lag caused by parental leave is normally not, on its own, an objective reason for a pay difference.

previousActions.title: Previous actions
previousActions.question: How were the measures planned in the previous pay mapping carried out?
previousActions.helper: The documentation must evaluate whether last year's planned measures were carried out and whether they had the intended effect.

equalWork.title: Equal work groups
equalWork.body: Groups are formed from what people actually do at work, not their job titles. Every pay difference in each group is analyzed here, no matter how small it looks: the 5% and 10% flags below are only this tool's own way of ordering what needs attention first, not a legal threshold.
equalWork.empty: No equal-work groups need documentation in this pay mapping.

equivalentWork.title: Women-dominated groups
equivalentWork.body: A group counts as women-dominated when at least 60% of it is women, a guideline from the Swedish Equality Ombudsman (DO), not a number written into law. For each such group, this chapter compares its pay against jobs the evaluation weighs as equally valuable or lower, but which still pay more.
equivalentWork.empty: No women-dominated groups have higher-paid comparisons in this pay mapping.

review.finishActionsNote: Pay adjustments, cost estimate and the three-year time plan are added in the action plan.
review.cycleBody: A pay mapping runs on an annual cycle: investigate the pay, analyze the differences, act on what you find, and follow up next year. This journey covers investigate and analyze; the actions themselves are gathered in the action plan afterward.

methodAppendix.methodologyBody: Roles are evaluated criterion by criterion on a 0 to 5 scale. Criterion weights sum to a fixed point budget; the role score is normalized to 0 to 100 and the level is derived, never set by hand. Ratings are hidden until every criterion is scored. Every change is recorded in the audit log. Roles describe work, never a person.

help.criterionBody: A criterion is something every role is evaluated against, like scope or complexity. Its 0 to 5 evaluation scale describes what each rating means; separately, its weighting decides how much it counts in the overall result.
help.anchorsLabel: How does the evaluation scale work?
help.anchorsBody: This is the 0 to 5 scale a role is evaluated against on this criterion. Each step describes what a role looks like there: write them concrete and role-focused, clearly increasing from 0 (not present) to 5 (the strongest reasonable expression), so two assessors reading the same job profile land on the same rating. This scale is about how a role is rated, not how much the criterion counts: that is its separate weighting.
help.anchorRoleBody: An anchor role is a reference role your organization has assessed and agreed on. Use the few you designate (2 to 5 is usually enough) to sanity-check other assessments: the comparison supports a decision, it never replaces the assessment. Anchor roles are whole roles; the evaluation scale on each criterion describes the ratings.
help.trackBody: A track is the kind of job, for example individual contributor or manager. It is set on the role and groups roles with the same kind of responsibility. It says nothing about seniority or how high the role lands.
help.familyBody: A role family groups roles that share the same kind of work, like Engineering or Sales. Families organize the role register and the results filter; they never affect the weighting.
help.weightingBody: Weighting is how much influence each criterion has on role valuation and, all else equal, on relative pay. It is not a verdict on whether a criterion is good or modern. Each criterion gets 1 to 5 weight points from one fixed budget for the whole model, so giving one more means the others count relatively less. New criteria start at the neutral 3.
help.scoreLabel: How are the weighting and level computed?
help.scoreBody: Every criterion is rated 0 to 5 and weighted by its weight points; the total is normalized to a fixed 0 to 100 scale, the weighting. The level then follows automatically from the weighting via the model's level thresholds, where level 1 is the highest. Neither can be set by hand.
help.blindRatingBody: Pick the step that best matches what the role requires, not how the current employee performs. Ratings, weighting, and level stay hidden until the last criterion so each one is judged on its own; the result appears as soon as every criterion is rated.
help.familiesReviewBody: A role family groups roles that share the same kind of work, like Engineering or Sales; families organize the register and never affect the weighting. A track is the kind of job, for example individual contributor or manager; it says nothing about seniority.
help.pendingLevelLabel: Why does a role have no level yet?
help.pendingLevelBody: A role gets a level only after every criterion is rated. Until the assessment is complete it has no weighting and no level, so it waits in this list.
help.contributionLabel: What do the bars and percentages show?
help.contributionBody: The percentage is each criterion's share of this role's total weighting (your rating times the criterion's weight in the model), so the criteria add up to 100%. The bars are scaled to the biggest contributor, so the top one fills the row.
help.twoFactorBody: Two-step verification adds a second check when you sign in, on top of your password: a code from an authenticator app or sent to your email. A stolen password alone then can't open your account. It is required for everyone on blueprnt.
help.changeEmailLabel: How does changing your email work?
help.changeEmailBody: Changing your email is a two-step process to keep your account secure. First, a confirmation link goes to your current address so only you can authorise the change. Then a verification link goes to your new address to confirm you own it. The change only takes effect once both links are clicked.
help.orgCurrencyBody: The currency your organization uses for pay. It defaults from your country and is used wherever amounts are shown. Changing it does not convert any existing values.
help.orgLanguageBody: The organization's default language, used for things like invitation emails when a member has not chosen their own. Each person can still pick their own display language.
help.methodAppendixBody: An exportable document with your criteria, weights, rationale, and bias review as compliance evidence.
help.biasReviewBody: A per-criterion check of gender and bias risk with a mitigating action. It shows the model is designed to reduce bias.
help.criterionRationaleBody: Why this criterion belongs in the model: its purpose, why it's relevant, and any overlap with others. It documents the objective basis the pay-transparency directive requires.
help.methodPurposeBody: What this criterion measures and the outcome it captures.
help.methodWhyRelevantBody: Why this criterion is relevant to the work's value, and why it is gender-neutral.
help.methodOverlapBody: Any overlap with other criteria, so the same thing is not weighted twice.
help.methodBiasRiskBody: The risk that this criterion over- or under-values gender-coded work, for example favouring visible mandate or budget size over actual complexity and responsibility.
help.methodBiasCommentBody: What you considered in the bias check and what you found.
help.methodBiasActionBody: The mitigating action taken to reduce the risk, such as reworded step descriptions or adjusted weighting.
help.classifySeniorityBody: Seniority is the individual's rank within the role's track, for example Senior or Lead. It is set per person, not on the role itself, and is used in pay-equity analysis to compare people in equivalent positions.
help.fteAdjustedBody: Part-time pay is scaled up to its full-time equivalent before comparing. A person working 80% with a monthly pay of 40,000 is shown as 50,000, so everyone is compared on full-time terms.
help.payMappingBody: A pay mapping (Swedish: lönekartläggning) is a frozen snapshot of your pay, roles and demographics at a point in time. All equal-pay analysis runs against the frozen copy, never live data, so the numbers cannot shift under you.
help.referenceDateBody: The date the snapshot represents. It is set to today when you start the mapping.
help.payGapEqualWorkBody: People doing the same job at the same seniority (Swedish: lika arbete). We compare the average pay of women and men in each such group.
help.payGapEquivalentWorkBody: Roles that the evaluation weighs equally (Swedish: likvärdigt arbete) land in the same level. This is the overall pay gap between women and men within that level, shown as context alongside the specific comparison above.
help.womenDominatedBody: A group counts as women-dominated when at least 60 percent of it is women. Swedish law requires comparing these groups with jobs the evaluation weighs as equally valuable or lower, but which pay more: a woman-dominated job should not be paid less than a job worth the same or less.
help.payGapFlagsBody: The flag is the pay gap between women and men in the group: over 10% needs action, 5-10% is worth watching, under 5% is fine. Groups with only one gender show no gap: there is no comparison to make.
help.equalityClockBody: The pay gap shown as time: the share of an 8-hour working day that the lower-paid gender works without matching pay. It is derived from the average gap, not a schedule.
help.headlineGapBody: The average pay gap between all women and all men in the survey (FTE-adjusted total pay). A positive value means women earn less. It is a whole-population figure, so it is shown even when individual groups are small.
help.payQuartilesBody: Everyone with a salary is ranked by pay and split into four equal groups, from the lowest-paid quarter to the highest. If women cluster in the lower quartiles and men in the upper, pay levels are unevenly distributed (a glass-ceiling pattern).
help.payGapReasonsBody: Swedish law requires an objective reason, for example market conditions or experience, for every pay difference between comparable groups. Pick the factors that apply and elaborate in the text field.
help.payGapDotPlotLabel: What does the dot plot show?
help.payGapDotPlotBody: Each dot is one person's pay in this group, on the group's primary measure: FTE-adjusted base salary (or total compensation when the group's difference sits in variable pay). The women's row sits above the men's, the dashed lines mark each gender's average, and the shaded band between them is the pay gap in kronor and percent. Hover a dot to see who it is and how far they sit from the men's average.
help.payGapMemberDiffBody: The person's FTE-adjusted pay minus the average of the men in this group, on the group's primary measure. A negative value means the person earns less than the men's average; a positive value means more. Part-time salaries are grossed up to full-time equivalents so the comparison is like for like.
help.payGapScatterBody: Each dot is one person, plotted by age or tenure against FTE-adjusted total pay. Pay can differ for objective, non-discriminatory reasons such as age or seniority: use this view to check for such a pattern before concluding a gap is unexplained. The scatter also makes pay dispersion visible: the law's analysis looks at differences in spread between the groups being compared, not only their averages.
help.payGapGateLabel: What does completing the pay mapping do?
help.payGapGateBody: Every equal-work group with a pay gap, and every women-dominated group with a higher-paid comparison, must be marked done with a documented reason before the pay mapping can be completed. This is the statutory documentation Swedish law requires.
help.collaborationBody: Collaboration (Swedish: samverkan) means cooperating with employees and their union representatives at every step of the pay mapping (Diskrimineringslagen 3 kap. 11 §). If your organization is bound by a collective agreement, the union representatives have a right to the information they need to take part (12 §).
help.genderPureBody: A pay mapping compares women's pay against men's. A group where everyone shares a gender has no such comparison to make, so it carries no flag, no documentation duty, and no place in the statutory report. It is kept here because internal pay dispersion and outliers are still worth understanding: a wide spread inside one job can point at pay-setting that would show up as a gender gap the moment the group's composition changes.
help.womenAheadLabel: Why are these not in the main flow?
help.womenAheadBody: The statutory duty targets pay differences to women's disadvantage. When the women in a group are at or above the men's average, there is nothing to explain or act on, so the group leaves the main flow rather than filling it with green rows. The figures stay here as analytical information.
help.analysisProgressBody: The count covers the steps that must be documented before the pay mapping can be completed: the collaboration record, the pay-practice review, every equal-work group with a pay difference to the women's disadvantage, and every women-dominated group with a higher-paid comparison. Analyses that carry no documentation duty are not counted.
